gaps.criterion: A known contact revisiting pricing merges, rescores and pauses nurture
gaps.gap: The DECISION is complete and tested end to end: pricing_revisit from an identifiable contact classifies as MERGE at high priority, and the action set names merge_into_existing_record, rescore, pause_generic_nurture and create_urgent_owner_task. Verified live. What is NOT built is the EXECUTION of those actions - nothing yet performs the merge, calls sdk-lead-scoring to rescore, or tells sdk-sequence to pause the nurture. The task is scoped as a policy engine ('ONE explicit configurable decision rather than scattered conditionals') and its endpoint returns the decision plus reasoning, so deciding is the deliverable; but a reader of the criterion could reasonably expect the pause to actually happen. Executing them needs sdk-lead-scoring and sdk-sequence wiring that is not in this task, and stubbing it would produce a call site that reports success while nothing paused - worse than the honest gap, because a nurture sequence still running at somebody actively evaluating is exactly what the criterion exists to prevent.
